chapter_name: The Sermon at Benares and Poems
learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the profound spiritual lesson by Gautama Buddha about the inevitability of death and grief, and explore W.B. Yeats' poem on superficial vs. true love.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Siddhartha Gautama, a royal prince shielded from suffering, accidentally sees a sick man, an aged man, a funeral procession, and a begging monk. Deeply moved, he leaves his royal life to seek enlightenment. He attains it under a Peepal tree (the Bodhi Tree) and becomes 'The Buddha' (The Awakened One). He gives his first sermon at the holy city of Benares.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🌱 Kisa Gotami and the Mustard Seed
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Kisa Gotami’s only son dies. Mad with grief, she asks everyone for medicine to revive him. A man directs her to Buddha. Buddha tells her he will cure the boy if she brings a handful of mustard seeds, but with one condition: the seeds must come from a house where no one has ever died.

Kisa goes from door to door but cannot find a single house untouched by death. She realizes that death is common to all. Buddha teaches her that weeping and grieving will not bring the dead back; it will only make one sick and pale. Peace of mind comes only by accepting the reality of death and overcoming sorrow.

main_concepts.concept_title: 👱‍♀️ For Anne Gregory (Poem by W.B. Yeats)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: A conversation between a young man and Anne Gregory. The man says her beautiful yellow hair (honey-coloured ramparts) traps young men in love. Anne says she can dye her hair brown, black, or carrot so men love her for 'herself alone' (inner beauty) and not her hair. The poet concludes that only God can love a person purely for their soul, not their physical appearance.

fun_activity.title: 👱‍♀️ The Hair Dye Test
fun_activity.instructions: In 'For Anne Gregory', Anne says she can change her hair color to black or brown to prove that looks don't matter. In today’s world of Instagram filters and makeup, people focus heavily on physical appearance. The poem reminds us of a harsh truth: humans naturally fall for outer beauty first. Only God loves us unconditionally for who we are inside!

exam_tips: 📌 What was the purpose of Buddha sending Kisa Gotami door-to-door for mustard seeds? (He wanted her to realize practically, rather than just telling her verbally, that death is a universal truth and no family is immune to it).
📌 Explain the comparison: 'As ripe fruits are early in danger of falling, so mortals when born are always in danger of death.' (Life is fragile and death is guaranteed).
📌 In the poem, what do 'honey-coloured ramparts' refer to? (Anne Gregory's beautiful blonde hair that acts like a wall/trap capturing young men's hearts).
quick_recap: ⭐ The Bodhi Tree is located in Bodh Gaya. 'Bodhi' means awakening or enlightenment.
⭐ Buddha says that drawing out the 'arrow of lamentation' (giving up weeping and complaining) is the only way to obtain peace of mind.
⭐ W.B. Yeats states that an old religious text proves only God loves us for ourselves alone, not humans.
